correctness.rationale: The complete general proof derives cumulants from conditional Gaussianity, the Markov two- and three-time functions, and explicit integrals. The fourth-cumulant ratio is strictly monotone because H'(z)>0 follows from 2 cosh(z)>2+z^2, valid for all z>0. Algebra then recovers p, delta, diffusivities, and rates uniquely; an open one-parameter physical family establishes exact second/fourth indistinguishability. A topological argument verifies the continuous-observation lower bound. An independent generator-based moment integration and inverse checker completed 802 deterministic assertions. Finite checks supplement but are not relied upon as the proof.

value.rationale: The exact small observation design answers a motivated identifiability question for a hidden fluctuating medium: only four preselected scalar population cumulants at two observation durations are sufficient, and the complete second/fourth-order time courses still leave a continuous ambiguity. The constructive global monotone inverse matters independently of existing forward occupation-time transforms, especially because the hidden rates and diffusivities are not separately observable from mean-square displacement alone. Value is structural; no finite-sample performance is asserted.
